@graph.description: Psyllium is the soluble fiber from the husks of Plantago ovata seeds, best known as a bulk-forming laxative. Because it forms a viscous gel that binds bile acids, it also affects blood lipids: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found that psyllium supplementation lowered LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B versus control, with roughly 10 grams per day a commonly studied dose. Psyllium should be taken with ample water and separated in time from other medications, whose absorption its gel can slow.
